hobbies: Long-distance trail running, restoring vintage synthesizers, and weekend pottery.

experiences.description: I lead frontend architecture for a customer-facing analytics suite, owning the component library and the patterns the rest of the team builds on. A big part of the role is mentoring two mid-level engineers and steering technical reviews so we keep the codebase consistent. I also partner closely with design to make sure what ships actually matches the intent.

Built and maintained the web client for a subscription commerce product used by tens of thousands of shoppers. I drove a migration off an aging stack onto a modern component model, which cut our build times and made onboarding faster. I owned accessibility work and helped set the team's testing conventions.

Worked on dashboards and configuration screens for an internal operations platform. My focus was untangling a sprawling state-management layer into something predictable and easy to reason about. I collaborated with backend engineers to redesign the contracts between our services and the client.

My first software role, building screens for a content management tool and fixing a steady stream of UI defects. I learned how to read a design spec, ask the right clarifying questions, and ship reviewed code on a regular cadence. Over time I took on small features end to end and started reviewing peers' pull requests.

projects.title: Shelfwise Storefront Refresh
projects.summary: A ground-up rebuild of the storefront experience for a consumer goods retailer, focused on speed and a cleaner browsing flow. I owned the interface work and coordinated tightly with merchandising and support stakeholders to keep everyone aligned. The result was a noticeably faster catalog and far fewer checkout drop-offs.

projects.title: Tenant Cloud Console
projects.summary: A self-service console that lets property managers provision and monitor their cloud-hosted units. I built the frontend that surfaced complex provisioning state in a way non-technical operators could follow. It bridged several backend services behind a single coherent interface.
